newsitem.title: ITALY: Chirac remarks almost wrecked Italy summit-sources.
newsitem.headline: Chirac remarks almost wrecked Italy summit-sources.

text.p: Italy almost called off a summit with France after President Jacques Chirac on Tuesday cast doubt on Italy's ability to be among the first countries to join Europe's planned single currency, political sources said.

One source told Reuters that the October 3-4 summit in Naples was "about to be scrapped" before Chirac issued a subsequent statement saying he ardently hoped Italy would succeed in joining economic and monetary union from 1999.

Chirac incensed Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government when he told businessmen in northern France on Tuesday morning that "it may take a little bit longer for those who are further behind, like Italy" to join the planned currency union.
Prodi summoned the French ambassador to Italy, Jean-Bernard Merimee, for an explanation of the remarks. Chirac then told a news conference in the northern French town of Arras:
"I believe the Italian government is fully determined to do everything, as it has shown in its budget, to be in the first wave of countries to join the euro. I ardently hope it will succeed".

The sources said Prodi had been adamant that the summit, which begins on Thursday night, could not go ahead if Chirac's initial statement stood. "Prodi's line was either he withdraws or we cancel" the trip to Naples, one of the sources said.
